replay: Rust: the config watcher is mixdog-core-config config/watch.rs:84 (it reloads the config file on a change) and the change feed is config/mod.rs:370 (pub fn changes). The channel reload entries are ChannelLifecycle::reload_config (mixdog-services channels/runtime.rs:393, trait channels/tools.rs:15, called from tools.rs:93 and from ServiceChannels::reload, daemon domain_seams/agent_effects.rs:60) -> ChannelRuntime::reload_runtime (runtime.rs:316, serialised by reload_gate :318). Checked by search of the daemon and services crates: NO consumer of config.changes() reloads the channel runtime on an external write (compose_flip.rs:801 passes the feed to the agents section, not to channels), so cases 55 and 75 (every external write reloads; only channels/voice sections reload) are work for the Rust side (rustWork). Case 92 cannot be driven as recorded (see rustWork): the replay compares the final config and the announcements after two writes. The files recorded are Node's config.json bytes for the Rust writer to equal
rustWork: Case 92 cannot be driven in Rust: Node lets two loads settle in reverse order (load #2 applies, load #1 is discarded), while the Rust core serialises reloads (mixdog-services channels/runtime.rs:318 reload_runtime, reload_gate), so load #2 cannot finish before load #1. What a client observes in Node, and what the replay compares: two writes (revision 101, then 102) start two loads in that order; when #2 resolves first, the config becomes {revision: 2} and exactly one set of announcements follows, in this order: setConfig({revision: 2}), scheduler.reloadConfig(schedules [], {restart: true}), syncWebhookAndEventRuntime({reload: true}); when #1 resolves last nothing is announced and the config stays {revision: 2}. So the newest write wins and is announced once, the older result is never applied. The Rust replay compares the final config and the announcements after both writes, not the interleaving
